info.bio: Misfits es un grupo musical de horror punk y hardcore punk formado en 1977 en la ciudad de Lodi, Nueva Jersey, liderado originalmente por el cantante Glenn Danzig y el bajista Jerry Only. La banda está enlazada al hardcore además de estar estrechamente relacionada por géneros como el punk rock, heavy metal, el rock and roll. Misfits siempre ha mostrado afinidad con el público del heavy metal, debido a que sus letras y su actitud son diferentes de los que tenían los grupos de punk anteriores.

scenes.name: Punk y hardcore
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El punk empieza en Inglaterra en 1975-76 y llega a California cuatro años después; de él sale el hardcore, fuerte en ambas costas estadounidenses y muy parecido al thrash naciente. Su código es el contrario del heavy: cualquiera puede tocar, voz plana sin emoción, igualdad entre fans y músicos frente a los guitar heroes. Grupos como los Misfits, llamados indistintamente horror metal y horror punk, muestran que la mezcla es posible; el thrash será un bricolage de segundo orden entre ambos códigos contradictorios.

scenes.name: Hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

podcast.title: Formation and Longevity
podcast.body: Glenn Danzig founded the Misfits around 1976 and kept the band active for six years, during which they developed their unique blend of hardcore, horror movie aesthetics, and metal. "The main guy was Glenn Danzig, who started the band somewhere around 1976, armed with his own indie record label. Danzig kept the Missfits going for six years, blending hardcore with horror movies and metal."

xref.title: Brand Repositioning
xref.body: "The Black Album" initiated a "careful repositioning" of the Metallica brand. While remaining metal, they began emphasizing their identity as music for "outsiders and misfits," allowing them to "kind of qualifies as alternative" and access a broader audience akin to Nirvana, Soundgarden, and Pearl Jam. "It was also the start of a careful repositioning of the Metallica brand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cousin Tracy Bradford's Punk Introduction
xref.body: His non-blood relative "cousin," Tracy Bradford, who was two years his senior and lived in Evanston, Illinois, introduced him to authentic punk rock culture. She appeared in bondage pants and motorcycle boots with an anti-P.C. t-shirt, showcasing a record collection including first singles from Misfits and Minor Threat, and connected him to the underground network of fanzines and show flyers from across the country. "She had an antiposti t-shirt and two's punk. I was just like, oh my God, I was so into it."

xref.title: Kennewick, Washington Background
xref.body: Nate Mendel grew up in Kennewick, a small town in Eastern Washington State, where there was "really no music happening." This lack of a local scene likely contributed to his and his friends' gravitating towards punk rock, seeing themselves as "misfits" drawn to something different. "Eastern Washington State. Okay. It's tiny little town out in the desert. What would you call? Kenwick."
